findings.title: Test never asserts send() actually fails with closed_error
findings.claim: The PR says send() fails with closed_error from then on, but the try/catch (closed_error) block also passes if the send succeeds; the contract is only indirectly checked via put_after_close, which depends on the batch-flush poller running within 10 yields. BOOST_REQUIRE_THROW(..., rpc::closed_error) would actually pin the contract.

findings.title: Parent client's unflushed compressor frame left unexplained by the fix
findings.claim: The PR description says the same 141-byte compressor frame was sitting unflushed on both the stream connection and its parent client, but the fix only covers stream connections via stream_close(); it doesn't say whether the parent's pending flush is a separate bug or harmless.

findings.title: New _stream_closing flag adds a third lifecycle flag send() must check
findings.claim: _stream_closing joins _error, _sink_closed, _source_closed and _sink_closed_future, and send() must now check two flags; a can_send() predicate or a single state enum would keep future callers from forgetting one (possible Primitive Obsession or Data Clumps).

findings.title: Pass-through socket wrappers duplicate loopback_socket.hh implementations
findings.claim: About 60 lines of pass-through socket wrappers in rpc_test.cc:1877-1937 overlap with the implementations already in tests/unit/loopback_socket.hh (possible Duplicated Code).

findings.title: Ordering invariant on _outgoing_queue_ready enforced only by a comment
findings.claim: The claim that nothing else waits for _outgoing_queue_ready from here on is guaranteed only by a comment; any future writer of _outgoing_queue_ready, such as enqueue_zero_frame() at rpc.cc:877, has to independently know about it.

findings.title: stop() now blocks waiting for the outgoing queue to drain, undocumented
findings.claim: If the front entry is stuck in send_entry() because the peer isn't reading, stream_close() blocks until that write finishes, and stream sends have no timeout; this is arguably better than the old behavior but the PR doesn't mention it.

findings.title: Test can hang instead of failing on regression
findings.claim: The wait on close_entered_cv has no timeout, and release_close.set_value() is skipped if the hook throws anything other than closed_error, so a regression hangs until the ctest timeout rather than reporting a failure.

findings.title: hooks recorded via const_cast instead of mutable, inconsistent with existing style
findings.claim: The existing cfactory in the same file (rpc_test.cc:330) declares its state mutable instead of using const_cast; hooks should follow that existing style and be mutable too.

findings.title: Duplicate comments left after adding new \brief blocks
findings.claim: New /// \brief blocks were added above the old // send data Out... and // receive data In... comments (also at :384-392) without removing or merging the old lines, leaving two comments per class.

findings.title: Doc understates that dropping an unclosed sink crashes via assertion
findings.claim: "Dropping an unclosed sink is an error" understates that it's actually a SEASTAR_ASSERT crash in ~sink_impl (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:935); the doc should say so explicitly.

findings.title: Doc sentence about when the stream connection is shut down is inaccurate
findings.claim: "The stream's connection is shut down only once both halves are closed" is wrong: the connection is also shut down on a peer or IO error, and by abort_all_streams() when the parent client closes; text a few lines above already says this correctly.

findings.title: Reference taken into a vector that can be reallocated
findings.claim: auto& stream_send_empty_frame = client_factory.hooks.back() points into a vector that any later negotiation's push_back could reallocate; it's safe today but should be a copy instead of a reference.

findings.title: PR description issue references point at nonexistent/wrong-repo issues
findings.claim: "Fixes #3663" points at nothing since no #3663 exists in dkropachev/ironweave; the reference needs to be scylladb/seastar#3663, and the same applies to "Refs #3653".

findings.title: New text appended to an already overlong line
findings.claim: New text was appended to an already long line, while the rest of the file wraps at about 80 columns.

findings.title: Unclear helper names that don't convey their close-parking/late-put-recording behavior
findings.claim: test_sink_state and test_data_sink_impl (also at :1877) don't indicate that they park close() and record late put() calls.
